proposals.before: At the end of Song's Shengming era he began as Attendant at Court, then served as Rear Army aide, Minister of Works cavalry officer, and Central Commandant's army aide.
proposals.after: At the end of Song's Shengming era he began as Attendant at Court, then served as Rear Army aide, Minister of Works cavalry officer, and Grand Commandant's army aide.
proposals.reason: 太尉 is the Grand Commandant (Defender-in-chief), not a 'Central Commandant'; 中兵 marks the inner-troops staff, not 'central' as a commandant's title.

proposals.before: At the end of Song's Shengming era he first entered office as Attendant at Court, and passed through Rear Army Aide, Cavalry of the Minister of Works, and Central Commandant's Army Aide.
proposals.after: At the end of Song's Shengming era he first entered office as Attendant at Court, and passed through Rear Army Aide, Cavalry of the Minister of Works, and Grand Commandant's Inner Troops Aide.
proposals.reason: Same 太尉 mistranslation as in the idiomatic line: 太尉 is Grand Commandant, not Central Commandant.

proposals.before: At Ying city Mao advanced to pacify Jiahu, defeated Guangziqin and Wu Ziyang, took tens of thousands of heads, and returned to report victory at Hanchuan.
proposals.after: At Ying city Mao advanced to pacify Jiahu, defeated Guang Ziqin and Wu Ziyang, took tens of thousands of heads, and returned to report victory at Hanchuan.
proposals.reason: 光子衿 is the personal name Guang Ziqin; the fused English 'Guangziqin' obscures the surname/given-name split.

proposals.before: When bandits burned Divine Tiger Gate, Mao rushed his men to East Yiji Gate; though shot at, he spurred forward and the bandits fled.
proposals.after: When bandits burned Divine Tiger Gate, Mao rushed his men to the East Side Gate; though shot at, he spurred forward and the bandits fled.
proposals.reason: 東掖門 is the palace East Side/Flank Gate (掖門). 'Yiji' is not a reading of 掖.

proposals.before: When bandits burned Divine Tiger Gate, Mao led his command to East Yiji Gate to answer the alarm; shot by bandits, he leapt his horse forward and the bandits turned and fled.
proposals.after: When bandits burned Divine Tiger Gate, Mao led his command to the East Side Gate to answer the alarm; shot by bandits, he leapt his horse forward and the bandits turned and fled.
proposals.reason: Same 東掖門 error: 掖 is ye 'side/flank', not 'Yiji'.

proposals.before: He was also made Pacify the Army General and enfeoffed as Duke of Wangcai with two thousand three hundred households.
proposals.after: He was also made General Who Stabilizes the Army and enfeoffed as Duke of Wangcai with two thousand three hundred households.
proposals.reason: 鎮軍將軍 is Zhenjun / 'stabilize/garrison the army', not 'Pacify the Army' (which would be 征 or 平).

proposals.before: He was given the additional title Pacify the Army General and enfeoffed as Duke of Wangcai county with a fief of two thousand three hundred households.
proposals.after: He was given the additional title General Who Stabilizes the Army and enfeoffed as Duke of Wangcai county with a fief of two thousand three hundred households.
proposals.reason: Same 鎮軍/Pacify mistranslation as in the idiomatic line.

proposals.before: His father Xinbei was a Song general who rose to Pacify the Barbarians General and inspector of Xuzhou.
proposals.after: His father Xinzhi was a Song general who rose to General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians and inspector of Xuzhou.
proposals.reason: 父欣之 is Cao Xinzhi (欣之). The English 'Xinbei' is not a reading of 欣之; 征虜 is 'campaign against the barbarians', not merely 'Pacify'.

proposals.before: His father Xinbei was a Song general who reached Pacify the Barbarians General and Xuzhou Inspector.
proposals.after: His father Xinzhi was a Song general who reached General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians and Xuzhou Inspector.
proposals.reason: Same 欣之/Xinbei error: 欣之 is Xinzhi.

proposals.before: Before he came of age, Xinbei sent him out of Xinye with one horse and a few followers; on the road several hundred Man bandits suddenly surrounded him.
proposals.after: Before he came of age, Xinzhi sent him out of Xinye with one horse and a few followers; on the road several hundred Man bandits suddenly surrounded him.
proposals.reason: 欣之 is again rendered Xinbei; the personal name is Xinzhi.

proposals.before: Before he had reached the weak-crown age, Xinbei at Xinye sent him out of the province with one horse and a few men; on the road he suddenly met several hundred Man bandits surrounding him.
proposals.after: Before he had reached the weak-crown age, Xinzhi at Xinye sent him out of the province with one horse and a few men; on the road he suddenly met several hundred Man bandits surrounding him.

proposals.before: When Prince of Poyang Xiao Zhen became inspector of Yongzhou, Jingzong was again made Pacify the Barbarians army aide and administrator of Fengyi, supervised troops south of Xian, and was promoted to Colonel of Garrison Cavalry.
proposals.after: When Prince of Poyang Xiao Jiang became inspector of Yongzhou, Jingzong was again made Campaign-against-the-Barbarians army aide and administrator of Fengyi, supervised troops south of Xian, and was promoted to Colonel of Garrison Cavalry.
proposals.reason: 鄱陽王鏘 is Xiao Jiang (鏘), not Xiao Zhen. 鏘 is not Zhen.

proposals.before: When Qi's Prince of Poyang Xiao Zhen held Yongzhou, Jingzong was again made Pacify the Barbarians Army Aide, concurrently Administrator of Fengyi, supervised military affairs south of Xian, and was promoted to Colonel of Garrison Cavalry.
proposals.after: When Qi's Prince of Poyang Xiao Jiang held Yongzhou, Jingzong was again made Campaign-against-the-Barbarians Army Aide, concurrently Administrator of Fengyi, supervised military affairs south of Xian, and was promoted to Colonel of Garrison Cavalry.
proposals.reason: Same 鏘/Zhen error: 鏘 is Jiang.

proposals.before: In Jianwu year two Tuoba Hong of Wei raided Zheyang; Jingzong was a flank commander, broke the line each time he charged, and was made Raids General for merit.
proposals.after: In Jianwu year two Tuoba Hong of Wei raided Zheyang; Jingzong was a flank commander, broke the line each time he charged, and was made Guerrilla General for merit.
proposals.reason: 遊擊將軍 is the Guerrilla / Mobile Assault General, not a 'Raids General'.

proposals.before: Gaozu, treating him as a meritorious minister grown lax and left unpunished, summoned him to be Protector of the Army.
proposals.after: Gaozu, because he was a meritorious minister, tabled the matter and did not punish him, and summoned him to be Protector of the Army.
proposals.reason: 以功臣寢而不治 means Gaozu shelved the impeachment because Jingzong was a meritorious minister, not that Jingzong himself was a minister 'grown lax'.

proposals.before: His father's elder brother Yuanjing had been Song Grand Marshal.
proposals.after: His father's elder brother Yuanjing had been Song Grand Commandant.
proposals.reason: 太尉 is Grand Commandant (Defender-in-chief), not Grand Marshal (大司馬).

proposals.before: His father's elder brother Yuanjing was Song Grand Marshal.
proposals.after: His father's elder brother Yuanjing was Song Grand Commandant.

proposals.before: When the Pacification Office was established, he was made aide of the Grand Marshal.
proposals.after: When the hegemon's headquarters was established, he was made aide of the Grand Commandant.
proposals.reason: 霸府 is the hegemon/prince's military government (Xiao Yan's pre-accession office), not a 'Pacification Office'; 太尉 is Grand Commandant.

proposals.before: When Liang arose they caught the day's last light and achieved their aims—rivaling Fang Hu and Shao Yi, their deeds cut into bell and tripod. Magnificent!
proposals.after: When Liang arose they caught the day's last light and achieved their aims—rivaling Fang Shu and Shao Hu, their deeds cut into bell and tripod. Magnificent!
proposals.reason: 方、邵 are the Zhou generals Fang Shu (方叔) and Shao Hu (召虎), not 'Fang Hu and Shao Yi'.

decisions.after: At the end of Song's Shengming era he entered office as an Attendant at Court, then served as Rear Army aide, cavalry officer to the Minister of Works, and aide for inner troops to the Grand Commandant.
decisions.reason: The proposal correctly separates 太尉, Grand Commandant, from 中兵, the inner-troops staff, but the revision makes that relationship explicit and improves the list of offices.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 歷後軍行參軍，司空騎兵，太尉中兵參軍

decisions.after: At the end of Song's Shengming era he first entered office as Attendant at Court, and went on to serve as Rear Army Aide, Cavalry Officer to the Minister of Works, and Inner Troops Aide to the Grand Commandant.
decisions.reason: 太尉 is Grand Commandant, while 中兵 describes the staff assignment. The revision preserves both elements of the office title in clearer literal English.

decisions.after: When the army reached Yingcheng, Mao advanced to pacify Jiahu, defeated Guang Ziqin, Wu Ziyang, and others, took tens of thousands of heads, and returned to report victory at Hanchuan.
decisions.reason: 光子衿 is Guang Ziqin, not the fused Guangziqin. The revision also restores the army as the subject of 師次 and retains 等, 'and others.'

sourceWitness.excerpt: 師次郢城，茂進平加湖，破光子衿、吳子陽等

decisions.after: When bandits set fire to Divine Tiger Gate, Mao led his men to answer the alarm at the East Side Gate. Though struck by an arrow, he spurred his horse forward, and the bandits turned and fled.
decisions.reason: 東掖門 is the palace's East Side Gate, not 'East Yiji Gate.' The revision also makes the sequence and the passive shooting construction natural in English.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 到東掖門應赴，爲盜所射，茂躍馬而進

decisions.reason: 掖門 is a side or flank gate of the palace. 'East Yiji Gate' is not a valid reading of 東掖門, and the proposed literal correction is accurate.

decisions.after: He was also made General Who Guards the Army and enfeoffed as Duke of Wangcai with two thousand three hundred households.
decisions.reason: 鎮 in this military title is 'guard' or 'garrison.' 'General Who Guards the Army' is clearer and more idiomatic than either the original 'Pacify' or the proposal's 'Stabilizes.'

decisions.after: He was given the additional title General Who Guards the Army and enfeoffed as Duke of Wangcai county with a fief of two thousand three hundred households.
decisions.reason: The literal field should render 鎮軍將軍 consistently as General Who Guards the Army while preserving the rest of the source structure.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 加鎮軍將軍，封望蔡縣公

decisions.after: His father, Xinzhi, was a general under Song who rose to General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians and Inspector of Xu Province.
decisions.reason: 欣之 is Xinzhi, not Xinbei, and 征虜 is a campaigning title. The revision also renders 徐州刺史 as Inspector of Xu Province in natural English.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 父欣之，爲宋將，位至征虜將軍、徐州刺史

decisions.after: His father Xinzhi was a Song general who reached the ranks of General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians and Inspector of Xu Province.
decisions.reason: The literal translation repeats the false reading Xinbei. 欣之 is Xinzhi, and the two final phrases are the offices to which he rose.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 欣之，爲宋將，位至征虜將軍、徐州刺史

decisions.after: Before Jingzong came of age, Xinzhi sent him out from Xinye with one horse and a few followers. On the road they were suddenly surrounded by several hundred Man bandits.
decisions.reason: 欣之 again names Xinzhi. Naming Jingzong once resolves the English pronoun chain without adding information absent from the biography.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 未弱冠，欣之於新野遣出州

decisions.after: Before he had reached the age of twenty, Xinzhi sent him out of the province from Xinye with one horse and a few men; on the road he suddenly encountered several hundred Man bandits who surrounded him.
decisions.reason: 欣之 is Xinzhi. The revision keeps the literal structure while expressing 弱冠 as the age of twenty and placing 'from Xinye' unambiguously.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 未弱冠，欣之於新野遣出州

decisions.after: When Xiao Qiang, Prince of Poyang, became Inspector of Yong Province, Jingzong was again made an Inner Troops Aide to the General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians and Administrator of Fengyi. He supervised military affairs south of Xian and was promoted to Colonel of Garrison Cavalry.
decisions.reason: The proposal correctly rejects Xiao Zhen but misreads 鏘 a second time: the name is Qiang, not Jiang. The revision also parses 征虜中兵參軍 as an inner-troops staff post.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 齊鄱陽王鏘爲雍州，復以爲征虜中兵參軍

decisions.after: When Qi's Prince of Poyang, Xiao Qiang, held Yong Province, Jingzong was again made Inner Troops Aide to the General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians, concurrently served as Administrator of Fengyi, supervised military affairs south of Xian, and was appointed Colonel of Garrison Cavalry.
decisions.reason: 鏘 is Qiang, not Zhen or Jiang. The revised literal field preserves the source's office sequence and the structure of 征虜中兵參軍.
遊擊將軍 is conventionally rendered Guerrilla General or General of Mobile Warfare. 'Raids General' is not an adequate rendering of the office.

decisions.after: Because Jingzong was a meritorious minister, Gaozu shelved the case without punishing him and summoned him to serve as Protector of the Army.
decisions.reason: 寢 is transitive here: Gaozu shelved the impeachment because Jingzong was a meritorious minister. It does not say that Jingzong had grown lax.

decisions.reason: 太尉 is Grand Commandant, whereas Grand Marshal would represent 大司馬. The proposed idiomatic correction is accurate.
The literal field likewise needs Grand Commandant for 太尉. The proposal makes the necessary correction without altering the sentence's structure.

decisions.reason: 霸府 is the pre-accession administration of the hegemon, not a Pacification Office, and 太尉 is Grand Commandant. The revision gives 從事中郎 a clearer office rendering.

decisions.reason: 方 and 邵 are shorthand for the Zhou generals Fang Shu and Shao Hu. The revision corrects both invented names and turns the appraisal into natural English.
